stories.headline: Apple smart glasses reportedly set for WWDC 2027 debut
stories.subtitle: Bloomberg reports Apple's first smart glasses will debut at WWDC 2027 and ship later that year — slimmer than Ray-Ban Meta Gen 2, with cameras and an agentic Siri, but no display. Expect "should I wait for Apple?" questions.

stories.headline: Google's Android XR glasses will blur faces from Gemini
stories.subtitle: Google says its Android XR glasses will blur bystanders' faces before images reach Gemini, and apps will be banned from real-time facial recognition or live-streaming from the cameras. Privacy is the rival's headline pitch.

stories.headline: XREAL Aura Android XR glasses start shipping
stories.subtitle: XREAL's Aura, the first wired display glasses running Google's Android XR, started shipping this week. The $1,099 launch price runs through December — the first display glasses on the Android XR shelf.

stories.headline: Android XR glasses get a 'Hey Gemini' hotword
stories.subtitle: Google's Android XR glasses answer to a 'Hey Gemini' hotword — hands-free voice control that isn't even on Android phones yet. It powers Samsung and Google's Intelligent Eyewear, on sale Dec. 10, so expect comparison questions.

stories.headline: Samsung and Google's Intelligent Eyewear opens for pre-orders at $395
stories.subtitle: Samsung and Google's first Android XR glasses opened pre-orders Nov. 12: Warby Parker frames from $395, Gentle Monster from $449, on sale Dec. 10. Camera and audio, no display, with Gemini built in — the first real rival to Ray-Ban Meta.
